sections.title: Executive investment summary: a mid-sized oncology formulator priced like a compounder

blocks.text: Beta Drugs makes and sells oncology medicines (tablets, capsules, liquid and lyophilised injections) from three plants in Baddi/Barotiwala (Himachal Pradesh) and Derabassi (Punjab) [F] (PPT Jul 2026) (RATING). It earns money in five ways: (1) its own 'Adley' brands sold to Indian oncologists and hospitals; (2) contract manufacturing (CMO/CDMO) for Indian pharma companies; (3) exports, mostly through government tenders in emerging markets; (4) oncology API sold to third parties; and (5) a small dermatology/cosmetology trading business [F] (PPT Jul 2026) (CALL May 2026). From April 2026 it also consolidates Nivian Life Sciences, a 66.09%-owned IVF brand company that outsources all manufacturing to 11 third parties [F] (AR2026 p.21) (PPT Jul 2026).

blocks.text: By geography, 81.6% of FY26 revenue was domestic (Rs314.0 cr) and 18.4% exports (Rs70.9 cr) [F] (AR2026 p.121). The FY26 export book split as LATAM 42%, APAC 32%, Africa 19% and MENA 7% [F] (PPT Jul 2026). In Q1 FY27, revenue was Rs125.5 cr: branded oncology Rs33.0 cr, Nivian about Rs15.1 cr, CMO Rs47.4 cr, exports Rs17.2 cr, API Rs8.3 cr and dermatology Rs4.5 cr [F] (PPT Jul 2026).

subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: Beta listed on the NSE SME (Emerge) platform in 2017 and moved to the NSE main board on 24 November 2025 [F] (PPT Jul 2026) (AR2026 p.18). Corporate-governance reporting applied for the first time from Q3 FY26, and the company reported only half-yearly until then [F] (AR2026 p.46) (CALL May 2026). No offer document or prospectus was available to us. Quarterly history before Q3 FY26 is therefore thin, and the earlier quarterly splits in our statements data are probably derived from half-year filings [AI]. No transcript of a Q1 FY27 earnings call was available, so the latest quarter is covered only by the July 2026 presentation [F] (PPT Jul 2026).

In its 25 September 2026 update, CRISIL says it is 'awaiting adequate information' from Beta to carry out its rating review and flags information-availability risk [F] (RATING). The only rated debt is Rs8 cr of bank facilities [F] (RATING). We read this as a disclosure-quality warning rather than a credit issue [AI].

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. **Valuation is far beyond every scenario.** The bull-case DCF value of Rs580.9 is 70.2% below the Rs1,950 share price, and the base case of Rs366.9 is 81.2% below it [F] (NUMBERS). The reverse DCF needs about 67% annual sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS).

2. **Guidance has repeatedly been missed.** FY26 was guided at 20-25% growth and 23-25% EBITDA margin [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The company delivered 6.2% growth and a 19.7% EBITDA margin [F] (AR2026 p.5). Second-half FY26 exports were guided above Rs100 cr [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) but came in at about Rs27.7 cr [E] (AR2026 p.121) (CALL Nov 2025).

3. **Exports are volatile and opaque.** Q1 FY27 exports fell 47% YoY to Rs17.2 cr [F] (PPT Jul 2026), below the Rs20-22 cr management had guided six weeks before quarter-end [MC] (CALL May 2026). Tender values, countries and customers are withheld [MC] (CALL May 2026).
4. **Organic growth is about 10%, not 25%.** Excluding Nivian's roughly Rs15.1 cr, Q1 FY27 revenue grew about 10% YoY [E] (PPT Jul 2026).

5. **Profits are not turning into free cash.** FCF was -Rs1 cr in FY25 and -Rs16 cr in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Cumulative five-year FCF of Rs17 cr compares with about Rs175 cr of PAT [E] (NUMBERS). Working-capital days rose from 80 to 97 over FY24-FY26 [F] (NUMBERS).

6. **Accounting and audit signals are weak.** The audit is done by a small firm for a Rs4.2 lakh standalone fee, on two-year terms [F] (AR2026 p.13, p.62). The consolidated audit report contains no key audit matters [F] (AR2026 p.107-108). The EPS note says there were 'no dilutive potential equity shares' while 6.65 lakh CCDs were outstanding [F] (AR2026 p.129, p.58). The notes also contradict each other on MSME dues [F] (AR2026 p.121, p.143).

7. **Promoter behaviour needs explaining.** The main promoter holder, Mrs Neeraj Batra, held 1.85 lakh fewer shares at March 2026 than a year earlier [E] (AR2026 p.118). The two promoter directors each drew Rs1.51 cr from Beta and are also paid the same amounts in the subsidiary Adley Formulations [F] (AR2026 p.102, p.173).

8. **Credit-information red flags.** Brickwork classified the company as non-cooperative in June 2020 [F] (RATING). The FY26 annual report still lists a Brickwork 'A-' rating [F] (AR2026 p.59). CRISIL is now 'awaiting adequate information' [F] (RATING).

9. **Diversification drift and dilution.** The company has added dermatology, fillers, IVF and biosimilar talks while core CDMO grew 1% in FY26 [F] (PPT Jul 2026) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The share count rose from 96.1 lakh to about 1.109 cr since March 2024 [F] (AR2026 p.118) (NUMBERS). An ESOP has been approved but not yet granted [F] (AR2026 p.18).

10. **Price-control exposure.** Carboplatin's NPPA ceiling of Rs2,850 sits close to an industry cost of Rs2,300-2,400 [MC] (CALL May 2026). Platin supplies were largely halted in H2 FY26 [MC] (CALL May 2026).

subsections.title: Key debates: what the market may be getting wrong

items: Is 25% growth back? Bull: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25.2% and EBITDA 39% [F] (PPT Jul 2026). Bear: about 15 points of that came from an acquisition, and exports halved [E] (PPT Jul 2026). Our read: the quarter was mix-driven and inorganic, not a broad recovery [AI].

Is CMO a dying low-margin line or a hidden asset? Management plans to shrink CMO from 39% to 13% of revenue by FY30 [MC] (CALL May 2026). Yet CMO grew 41% YoY in Q1 FY27 and remains the largest vertical [F] (PPT Jul 2026). CMO may be more volatile, and more important to absorbing overhead, than the Vision 2030 narrative implies [AI].

Is the balance sheet a strength? Bull: about Rs104 cr of cash remains after the Nivian cash consideration [E] (AR2026 p.117, p.18). Bear: Rs41.0 cr of the fixed-asset base is land, part of which management now plans to sell, and FY26 FCF was negative [F] (AR2026 p.114) (CALL May 2026) (NUMBERS).

Does the DCF understate value? Yes, partly. Its equity bridge deducts Rs148 cr of borrowings, including Rs110 cr of CCDs since converted into shares that are already in its 1.109 cr share count, and gives no credit for cash [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.119). Even so, the correction is an order of magnitude smaller than the gap between the base-case equity value of Rs406.8 cr and the Rs2,162 cr market cap [AI] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: The market appears to price Beta as a high-growth specialty-oncology compounder with near-certain export and regulated-market upside [AI] (NUMBERS). Our reading of the documents is different. Beta is a well-run but mid-scale Indian oncology formulator with one strong franchise (domestic brands growing about 20%) [F] (PPT Jul 2026). That franchise is wrapped in a lumpy CMO book, a tender-driven export arm that has missed guidance in two consecutive periods, and a newly bought IVF distributor [AI]. Earnings quality is respectable on CFO/PAT (0.87x over three years) but poor on free cash [F] (NUMBERS). Disclosure falls short of main-board norms: there are no audited segments, no customer data, no order book, and the credit agency is waiting for information [F] (AR2026 p.142) (RATING). If the business delivers management's Vision 2030 (Rs850-900 cr) [MC] (CALL May 2026), it would land between our base and bull DCF paths, and both still sit far below the current price [AI] (NUMBERS).

sections.title: Business model: a vertically integrated oncology formulator with three go-to-market channels

items: Step 1, KSMs and intermediates: mainly imported, largely from China [MC] (CALL May 2026). 60-70% of intermediates are China-sourced [MC] (CALL Nov 2024). An in-house intermediate plant is targeted to start by the end of Q3 FY27 [MC] (AR2026 p.5).

Step 2, API: Adley Lab (Derabassi; two lines of 60 TPA and 30 TPA) [F] (PPT Jul 2026). About 70% of the APIs used in the company's formulations are made in-house [MC] (AR2026 p.43). The presentation says '80%+' elsewhere [MC] (PPT Jul 2026), which is not reconciled.
Step 3, R&D and regulatory: NDDS formulations, dossiers and bioequivalence [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Disclosed R&D spend was Rs2.04 cr [F] (AR2026 p.25).
Step 4, formulation: Adley Formulations (Barotiwala) serves domestic branded and CMO; the Beta plant (Nandpur) is being repositioned for exports [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

Step 5, go-to-market: an oncology field force across hospitals; a separate derma team (69 territory managers) [MC] (CALL May 2026); CMO partners; export distributors and government tenders [MC] (AR2026 p.43).
Step 6, collection: receivables of 113 days and payables of 172 days of material cost [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: Management's segment margins put most value in domestic brands (35-36% EBITDA). Exports and API earn 20-21%, and CMO 17-18% [MC] (CALL May 2026). These margins are not audited: the accounts say the segments fall below Ind AS 108 thresholds [F] (AR2026 p.142). On management's figures, branded oncology at 32% of FY26 revenue would generate a little over half of group EBITDA [E] (PPT Jul 2026) (CALL May 2026). Value capture rests on prescriber relationships and cytotoxic manufacturing capability, not on IP: the company cites two patents [F] (PPT Jul 2026) [AI].

Fixed-asset turnover was 3.08x in FY26, down from 4.55x in FY24 [F] (NUMBERS). Land explains much of the fall: it rose from Rs1.9 cr to Rs41.0 cr of gross block over FY25-FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.114). The business is moderately capital-light on productive assets but working-capital heavy: inventories plus receivables of Rs193.6 cr are 50% of FY26 revenue [E] (AR2026 p.111). Nivian adds a fully outsourced, asset-light model [F] (PPT Jul 2026).

blocks.text: Most of the 135-180+ oncology SKUs are branded generics of off-patent molecules [MC] (CALL May 2026) (PPT Jul 2026). Price controls (NPPA) and tender pricing make them commodity-like at the molecule level [AI]. Differentiation is narrow: a handful of NDDS suspensions and RTU injectables, with one brand near Rs10 cr [MC] (CALL May 2026) and 'top 10 brands contribute more than 50%' of own-brand sales [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). CMO and API are capability-differentiated (cytotoxic containment) but price-negotiated [AI]. We classify roughly the CMO, export tender and API books (about 64% of FY26 revenue) as commodity-like, and part of the branded book as differentiated [E] (PPT Jul 2026).

subsections.title: Is the export mix shift strategy or noise?

blocks.text: The export share rose from about 16% in FY24 to 22% in FY25, then fell to 18% in FY26 and 14% in Q1 FY27 [E] (AR2026 p.121) (PPT Jul 2026). Management's strategy is to reach 30% of revenue by FY30 through regulated-market dossiers [MC] (CALL May 2026). So far, though, the observed mix is driven by the timing of a few tenders: 'the top five countries will contribute almost about 30% of the sales' [MC] (CALL May 2026). We classify the movement to date as mix noise, not delivered strategy [AI]. The stated number of countries served ranges from 20+ to 46+ across the same presentation and calls, and is not reconciled [F] (PPT Jul 2026) (CALL May 2026).

items: FX: the company does not hedge [F] (AR2026 p.59). Consolidated FX was a Rs0.24 cr loss in FY26, while the standalone accounts show a Rs0.22 cr gain [F] (AR2026 p.144, p.104). FX inflows of Rs67.7 cr (standalone) are naturally offset by about Rs36.5 cr of foreign-currency spend [F] (AR2026 p.26, p.144). One SIDBI loan is a USD term loan (Rs1.4 cr) [F] (AR2026 p.135).
Tariffs: the documents disclose no US exposure, and management says US entry is 2-3 years away at best [MC] (CALL Nov 2024). No tariff events are disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.42-45).

Trade policy and geopolitics: the chairman says FY26 export registrations were 'impacted due to geopolitical considerations' [MC] (AR2026 p.5). Five months of petroleum-derived inputs were stockpiled during the 2026 tensions [MC] (CALL May 2026). Exports go to sanctions-sensitive markets including Russia, Belarus, Syria, Yemen and Venezuela [F] (PPT Jul 2026), creating payment and compliance risk that is not discussed [AI].
India price control: NPPA caps on carboplatin forced platin supplies to stop in domestic markets [MC] (CALL May 2026).

blocks.text: All three plants sit in the Baddi-Barotiwala (Himachal Pradesh) and Derabassi (Punjab) belt [F] (PPT Jul 2026). Heavy rain in North India and two foreign audits cost 15-20 days of production in H1 FY26 [MC] (CALL Nov 2025), and a 10-day Mexico audit cost Rs7-8 cr of FY25 sales [MC] (CALL May 2025). We rate regional concentration as a real operational risk for a cytotoxic producer with no alternative sites [AI].

blocks.text: Utilisation is disclosed only for FY26, so there is no trend. The simple average of the three plants is about 72% [E] (PPT Jul 2026). blocks.text: Imports by country are not disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.144). Management says 60-70% of intermediates come from China [MC] (CALL Nov 2024) and that 'our main KSMs come from China' [MC] (CALL May 2026). The documents give only platin price episodes. Platin raw-material inflation cut margins to about 18% in FY24 [MC] (CALL Nov 2024). Carboplatin input cost of Rs2,300-2,400 against an NPPA ceiling of Rs2,850 made domestic supply uneconomic [MC] (CALL May 2026). Management says price rises are passed through 'from every division' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The evidence says pass-through is partial: price-controlled molecules could not pass costs through and were dropped, and platin gross contribution falls to 10-15% from 50-70% on other products [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Gross margin still rose from 52.7% to 55.5% in FY26 [E] (AR2026 p.112), through mix.

subsections.title: Structural versus temporary drivers by year

items: FY24 (margin down to 20%): platin input-cost spike, which is temporary [MC] (CALL Nov 2024); derma start-up losses, which are investment [MC] (CALL May 2025).
FY25 (21%): platin prices eased and growth shifted toward higher-margin exports and brands [MC] (CALL Nov 2024). Derma lost about Rs3 cr [MC] (CALL May 2025).

FY26 (20%): gross margin rose 2.8 points on mix (fewer platins, more brands) [E] (AR2026 p.112). It was absorbed by employee cost up 22.5% to Rs68.0 cr, legal and professional fees up 67% to Rs5.3 cr, and R&D consumables up from Rs0.8 cr to Rs3.6 cr [E] (AR2026 p.123-124). Revenue rose only 6.2% [F] (AR2026 p.17). Excluding derma, management puts oncology EBITDA at 20.6% [MC] (AR2026 p.5).

Q1 FY27 (22%): mix effects from branded oncology (+47%) and higher-margin CMO products, plus first-time Nivian consolidation [F] (PPT Jul 2026). Lower export share would normally dilute margin less than management's segment margins imply [AI].

blocks.text: Part of it is. The gross-margin step-up from 49.5% to 55.5% over FY24-FY26 is tied to exiting price-controlled platins and growing brands, which looks durable [E] (AR2026 p.112) [MC] (CALL May 2025). But it has not reached EBITDA: operating margin has been 20-21% for three years, against management's repeated 23-25% guidance [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL May 2025) (CALL Nov 2025). Only one quarter at 22% exists, and it includes an acquisition [F] (PPT Jul 2026). Our view: gross margin is structurally higher, operating margin is not yet shown to be [AI].

subsections.title: What drove the change: management versus evidence

blocks.text: Management says the receivables increase is 'only 4.5 days' and that 'keeping the volume in mind ... five days is nothing' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The evidence shows a larger shift. Receivable days rose 10 days in FY26 while revenue grew only 6% [F] (NUMBERS). Inventory days rose 32 days, partly from a deliberate stockpile of inputs [MC] (CALL May 2026) and a 70% rise in raw-material stock [E] (AR2026 p.116). CRISIL rates Rs5 cr of cash credit and notes group bank-limit utilisation of about 33% [F] (RATING). Management expects Rs7-10 cr of utilised working-capital lines in FY27 [MC] (CALL May 2026). Financial covenants are not disclosed. CRISIL's downgrade triggers include 'elongation of working capital cycle' [F] (RATING), and the FY26 trend is moving toward that trigger [AI].

blocks.text: Illustrative arithmetic only: Beta's FY26 branded oncology (Rs123.2 cr) is about 0.12% of an Indian oncology market of USD12 bn (about Rs1 lakh cr at roughly Rs85/USD) [E]. Most of the Indian oncology TAM is biologics, immuno-oncology and originator brands that Beta does not sell [AI]. items: Branded oncology = prescribers x brands x realisation: 1,500+ prescribers (Nov 2024), prescriber base up about 8% in H1 FY26, top 10 brands over 50% of sales [MC] (CALL Nov 2024) (CALL Nov 2025). The three-year delivered growth of about 20% is the best bottom-up anchor [F] (PPT Jul 2026).

sections.title: Final thesis

blocks.text: Beta has a real, growing domestic branded-oncology franchise (+20% a year for three years; +47% in Q1 FY27) [F] (PPT Jul 2026). It has vertically integrated cytotoxic manufacturing with spare capacity [F] (PPT Jul 2026), a second branded leg in IVF [F] (PPT Jul 2026), and a net-cash balance sheet after CCD conversion [E] (AR2026 p.117, p.119). If exports convert the 623-dossier pipeline and the KSM plant lifts gross margin, management's Rs850-900 cr Vision 2030 would put the business on a bull-case trajectory [MC] (CALL May 2026) [F] (NUMBERS).

At Rs1,950 the stock trades at about 3.4x the bull-case DCF value of Rs580.9 [E] (NUMBERS), and the reverse DCF needs about 67% annual growth [F] (NUMBERS). Delivery has deteriorated: 6% growth in FY26, export misses, about 10% organic growth in Q1 FY27, and negative FCF [F] (AR2026 p.17) (NUMBERS) [E]. Disclosure and accounting craftsmanship fall short of main-board standards, and the credit agency is waiting for information [F] (RATING) (AR2026 p.129, p.142).

sections.title: Research view

blocks.text: The Rs1,950 price is above all three DCF values: bear Rs135.6, base Rs366.9 and bull Rs580.9 [F] (NUMBERS). The gap is driven by the market capitalising a high-growth specialty-pharma narrative: Vision 2030, regulated exports, IVF and KSM integration [AI]. The documents show a mid-scale oncology formulator growing about 10% organically, at a 20% EBITDA margin, with weak free cash flow [E] (PPT Jul 2026) (NUMBERS). We issue no rating or price target.

For long-horizon investors the business is worth following for the branded franchise [AI]. The evidence base does not support the current valuation on any horizon we can model [AI]. We will re-review on: (1) Q2 FY27 results, to test the H1 export +30% guide and organic growth [MC] (CALL May 2026); (2) any disclosure of the EU GMP inspection outcome [MC] (CALL May 2026); (3) the next CRISIL rating action [F] (RATING); (4) Q3 FY27 results and KSM plant commissioning by end-Q3 FY27 [MC] (AR2026 p.5); and (5) the FY27 annual report, for segment, customer and auditor disclosures [AI].
